nodes.name: Potentiostatic Electrodeposition of CoCat
nodes.procedure: Electrolyte solution prepared by dissolving KH2PO4 and K2HPO4 in 2:3 mixture (total phosphate 0.1 mol L^-1), pH adjusted to 7.00±0.05. Added 5.0×10^-2 mol L^-1 Co(NO3)2·6H2O solution to give final [Co] = 5.0×10^-4 mol L^-1. CoCat films potentiostatically deposited on cleaned ITO/Mylar/Pt electrodes at 1.05 V vs NHE until desired charge density passed (typically 10 mC cm^-2). Electrodes cleaned with ethanol and MilliQ water prior use.

unit_operations.name: Buffer Preparation
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: dissolving KH2PO4 and K2HPO4 in a 2:3 mixture, with a total phosphate concentration of 0.1 mol L^-1. The pH of the buffer solution was adjusted to 7.00±0.05

unit_operations.name: Cobalt Addition
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: adding a 5.0×10^-2 mol L^-1 solution of Co(NO3)2·6H2O to the phosphate buffer to obtain a final cobalt concentration of 5.0×10^-4 mol L^-1

unit_operations.name: Electrode Cleaning
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: ITO-coated glass, ITO-coated Mylar, or platinum disks were used as the working electrode and were cleaned with ethanol and MilliQ water prior use

unit_operations.name: Potentiostatic Deposition
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: CoCat films were potentiostatically deposited onto ITO electrodes from this solution by applying 1.05 V versus the NHE until the desired charge density was passed, typically 10 mC cm^-2

nodes.description: OER chronoamperometry-CV stability testing in cobalt-free 0.1 M phosphate buffer (pH 7) across 0.85-1.50 V vs NHE

working_electrode.value: ITO-glass, ITO-Mylar, or Pt disk coated with CoCat

nodes.source_text: Chronoamperometry experiments (CA) were systematically repeated on freshly deposited CoCat films by applying a selected voltage for a 24 h period, with voltages chosen to be 50 mV steps from 0.85 to 1.50 V versus the NHE. Each set of CA experiments was interrupted at regular 30 min intervals to perform two CV cycles... The behavior can be broken into three voltage regimes...

nodes.description: OER stability in Co(II)-containing phosphate buffer (3-40 μM Co(NO₃)₂) primarily at 1.3 V vs NHE
nodes.source_text: Plots of Q_red versus time and catalytic current versus time for CoCat films at 1.3 V illustrate the overall effect of solvated cobalt ions... The number of redox-active Co ions increases with time for all Co-containing electrolyte solutions, approaching what appears to be a limiting value of nearly 400% growth at the highest concentration examined.

nodes.description: In operando CA-XANES tracking oxidation state and film growth at 1.3 V in 20 μM Co buffer

electrolyte.value: phosphate buffer + 20 μM Co(NO₃)₂ + 1 M KNO₃

nodes.source_text: The CA-CV cycle was repeated over an 8.5 h timeframe at the synchrotron using an applied voltage of 1.3 V in an electrolyte solution containing 20 μM Co(NO₃)₂. Full XANES spectra were acquired every 5 min... Over this timeframe, the cobalt-edge position and the catalytic current density remained stable, while the Co Kα fluorescence intensity increased.

nodes.description: EXAFS structural analysis after 24 h operation at 1.3 V vs NHE
nodes.source_text: XAFS results indicate a structural evolution... Peak (a) is comparable for all three samples, but peak (b) is substantially larger after the 24 h electrochemical conditioning process. Peaks (c-e) indicate medium range ordering within the lattice.

nodes.description: Tafel slope evolution during 48 h CA at 1.3 V in varied Co concentrations
nodes.source_text: The steady-state current densities measured for three freshly prepared CoCat films reveal a steady decrease in the measured Tafel slopes... In all cases, the Tafel slope increased from ca. 65 mV dec⁻¹ at the start... to ca. 75 and 85 mV dec⁻¹ after 24 and 48 h, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: TXRF quantifies the total cobalt content in CoCat films after 24 h operation, showing loss in cobalt-free solutions and growth with added Co²⁺ depending on voltage and concentration.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The amount of cobalt, potassium, and phosphorous in selected CoCat films was analyzed by dissolving them and performing total reflection Xray fluorescence spectroscopy (TXRF; Bruker Picofox spectrometer).

nodes.characterization_summary: In operando XANES tracks voltage-induced oxidation state changes and shows biexponential kinetics with time constants τ₁ and τ₂; full-edge spectra reveal stable average Co oxidation state during 8.5 h conditioning at 1.3 V.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In operando X-ray absorption near-edge spectroscopy (XANES) experiments indicate that the rate of oxidation of cobalt ions within CoCat is consistent across all electrolyte compositions and film thicknesses.

nodes.characterization_summary: EXAFS reveals structural evolution with growth in di-μ-hydr(oxo)-bridged Co-Co peak at 2.80 Å and development of medium-range order peaks at 3.38, 4.85, and 5.60 Å after 24 h operation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Fourier transform of EXAFS data also reveals similar structural evolutions for CoCat films operated in Co-free and Co-containing electrolyte solutions.

properties.description: Fourier Transform of k³-weighted EXAFS spectrum

nodes.characterization_summary: CVs at 20 mV/s show broad anodic wave from overlapping Co²⁺/Co³⁺ and Co³⁺/Co⁴⁺ transitions merged with OER; cathodic Q_red (3.13-3.92 mC/cm² initially) measures redox-active Co ions.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Cyclic voltammograms (CVs) at 20 mV s⁻¹ capture the characteristic behavior of CoCat films in neutral solutions (Figure 1A), where a broad anodic wave that is typically attributed to overlapping Co²⁺/Co³⁺ and Co³⁺/Co⁴⁺ transitions is merged with the OER currents.

nodes.characterization_summary: UV-vis spectroscopy on 10 mC/cm² CoCat films confirms cobalt concentration trends observed by TXRF and Q_red after operation under varied conditions.
nodes.evidence_snippet: UV-visible spectroscopy provides a third measure of cobalt ion concentration in the films and further confirms these results (Figure S1).

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM shows smooth surface morphology (<10 nm features) for fresh CoCat and Co-free operated films, but 50-500 nm surface nodes develop with 20 μM Co(NO₃)₂ operation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Electron micrographs show that operation under cobalt-free conditions has little effect on surface morphology, but the presence of solvated Co(NO₃)₂ results in increased surface roughness.

nodes.characterization_summary: Cryogenic XAFS at 20 K analyzes structural evolution of frozen CoCat films; confirms layered double hydroxide-like structure with characteristic peaks.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Ex situ measurements were performed in a liquid helium-cooled cryostat (Oxford Danfysik) at 20 K to analyze the structural evolution of CoCat via X-ray absorption fine structure spectroscopy (XAFS).
